# Results (generated by analysis.py)

> Source numbers come from the assessment brief and were not re-verified. Sections 5 and 6 use synthetic or invented inputs and show mechanisms, not findings about a real product.

## 1. Share-rate decomposition (source numbers, one assumption)

- Reported share rate, among opened reels only: **92%**
- Unopened reels: **~30%** (source says 'roughly')
- Shared / all generated reels = 0.92 x 0.70 = **64.4%** *(assumes an unopened reel is never shared)*
- Opened but not shared = 5.6%; unopened = 30%
- So the 'unlocked reach' from fixing everything is NOT 35.6%: about 5.6 points are reels that were opened and still not shared.

## 2. Sensitivity of the 64.4% headline

- Range over unopened 20-40% and 0-10% leak: **55.2% to 75.6%**.
- Takeaway: 'about 64%' is fair; '64.4%' implies precision the inputs do not have.

## 3. Editor funnel (source bounds)

- Opened editor: **6%**; finished among openers: **< 1%**; so finished overall **< 0.06%**.
- Stated survey demand was 58% (n = 210, 40 clubs). Survey and telemetry cover different groups, so the gap is suggestive, not exact.
- Illustration (SYNTHETIC cohort): per 100,000 accounts, at most 6,000 open the editor and fewer than 60 finish an edit.

## 4. The proposed pilot gate (Wilson lower bound >= 0.95 at n = 500 audited clips)

- Smallest passing count at n = 500: **485 correct** (97.0% observed) -> lower bound 0.9511.
- 500/500 correct -> lower bound 0.9924; 480/500 -> 0.9390 (fails).

## 5. Chance that a system with a given TRUE accuracy passes the gate (exact binomial)

| true accuracy | n=200 | n=500 | n=1000 | n=2000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 96% | 4% | 15% | 29% | 53% |
| 97% | 15% | 57% | 88% | 100% |
| 98% | 43% | 95% | 100% | 100% |
| 99% | 86% | 100% | 100% | 100% |

- Reading: at n = 500 a system that is truly 97% accurate passes only about half the time; 98% passes almost always.
- Implication: choosing n is a product decision about how much wrongly-delivered content the pilot will tolerate.

## 6. CCDR under two counting rules (SYNTHETIC cohort, invented rates)

- Cohort: 120 child-weeks. Invented outcome rates: zero-highlight 12%, wrong child 3%, held 6%, delivery failure 4%.
- Rule A (honest zero = miss, the current choice): CCDR = **75.8%**
- Rule B (honest zero = success): CCDR = **85.8%**
- Difference: 10.0 points, driven entirely by how common zero-highlight weeks are. A quiet-playing child is not a product failure, so Rule A can punish honest behaviour.
- This is the product decision flagged in docs/CLAIMS_AND_EVIDENCE.md (item D2). The rates are made up; only the mechanism is the finding.
